about: What verify_receipt.py promises about a receipt bundle, written down so tests come from the promise and not from the code (20 Oct 2026, after four review rounds on agentrust-io/integrations#350 each found a hole the code's own tests could not). Every entry is one piece of evidence in a bundle. 'delete' = what removing it must do; 'tamper' = what altering its value must do. Outcomes: 'strict-refuses' = with --require-approval the exit is never 0 (1 or 3); 'fails' = in the default run the exit is 1 (for 'delete', removing it is a failed check in the default run, and so in strict mode too). A new check in the verifier gets a row here first; a row that cannot be honoured is a bug in the verifier, not in this file. A row with 'keys': true runs with --keys and the key document named in keyDocument (2 Nov 2026): without a key document the verifier checks the bundle's keys only against themselves. A row may name its own 'fixture' (2 Nov 2026): the anchor-chain rows run on anchored.bundle.json, a receipt sealed on 29 Oct 2026 and fetched from in.xchk.io on 2 Nov 2026, the first fixture to carry anchor.proof (a batched Ravencoin anchor with its manifest path) and an OpenTimestamps proof upgraded to a Bitcoin block; the 17 Oct fixtures and the 20 Oct corpus predate batched anchoring and left all seven anchor guards unpinned (guard-mutation sweep, 2 Nov 2026). A fixture listed in defaultModeFixtures runs its genuine check in the default run, not strict mode, for the reason given there (3 Nov 2026).

defaultModeFixtures.anchored-unbatched.bundle.json: an UNBATCHED anchor (the transaction carries this seal hash itself, no manifest) with its raw transaction captured, so the unbatched OP_RETURN guard runs; every such receipt was anchored between 8 and 10 Aug 2026, before bundles carried the passkey assertion and before the ask-v1 challenge (18 Oct 2026), so strict mode refuses any of them by design (exit 3, nothing failed). This one is an allow record of Sean's agent in seal #505, anchored 10 Aug 2026, fetched from in.xchk.io on 3 Nov 2026 exactly as served (review of #350 by drk-ram, 2 Nov 2026: the unbatched branch had no fixture).
